title: 2.1.28 Rewrite It as if/else
description: Take a ternary used for its side effect and rewrite it as an if/else statement. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: book 2.1.7: 'Non-traditional Use of ?', Try It Now 2.1.8

steps.title: Read the misused ternary
steps.instructions: The comment below shows a ternary being used to run two different actions instead of picking a value: (loggedIn == "yes") ? console.log("Welcome back!"): console.log("Please log in.");

steps.title: Rewrite it with if/else
steps.instructions: Create a variable called loggedIn and set it to "yes" or "no". Write an if/else statement with the same behavior as the ternary above: log 'Welcome back!' when loggedIn is 'yes', log 'Please log in.' otherwise.

requirements.title: if checks loggedIn === yes and logs Welcome back
requirements.description: if statement compares loggedIn to 'yes' and logs a message containing 'Welcome back'. Help: 2.1.3 (If / Else if / Else)

requirements.title: else logs Please log in
requirements.description: the else branch logs a message containing 'Please log in'. Help: 2.1.3 (If / Else if / Else)
